purpose: Per CEO R280 P2: 'Don't send generic emails to 10 companies. Create 5 specific technical buyers and for each: why this technology matters to them, what existing product it interfaces with, what experiment they can run, what data they need to provide, what decision they can make after the experiment.' Objective: get a technical evaluation commitment, not $500K.
constitutional_basis: Article XXVI — no self-certification. The first buyer conversation is the first independent evidence event.
the_objective: Get ONE real engineer to say: 'Send me the package; we'll run it.' That is the first commercial evidence event. Not $500K. Not a sales pitch.

buyer_1_medtronic_codman.existing_product: Codman Certas (programmable valve with 7 pressure settings, but NO sensing, NO closed-loop control, NO prediction)
buyer_1_medtronic_codman.why_p_01_matters: Medtronic's Codman Certas is REACTIVE — surgeon manually adjusts pressure setting based on symptoms. P-01 V2 (if it survives V2 testing) offers AUTOMATED continuous control. This is the next-generation differentiator for their flagship shunt product.
buyer_1_medtronic_codman.what_experiment_they_run: Run the V2 simulator (10_V2_comparison.py) with their Codman Certas valve parameters (pressure settings 1-7, flow ranges, valve response time). Compare V2's continuous control vs their discrete 7-setting approach. 30 minutes of engineering time.
buyer_1_medtronic_codman.what_data_they_provide: (1) Codman Certas valve specifications (flow-pressure curves for each setting). (2) Their published or internal data on shunt obstruction rates in their patient population. (3) Their revision surgery cost structure (for the buyer economic questionnaire).
buyer_1_medtronic_codman.what_decision_they_make: After running the simulator: 'Does V2's continuous risk-limited control materially outperform our 7-setting discrete approach under realistic uncertainty?' If YES → technical evaluation conversation. If NO → 'Thank you, not interested.'
buyer_1_medtronic_codman.contact_strategy: LinkedIn to VP R&D, Neuroscience. Reference their Codman Certas product specifically. Offer to share simulator with their engineering team. No NDA needed to run the simulator.
buyer_1_medtronic_codman.probability_of_engagement: 15-25% (Medtronic is large, slow-moving, but has the most to gain from automated shunt control)

buyer_2_integra_lifesciences.existing_product: Codman Hakim Programmable Valve (mechanical programmable valve) + Integra NeuroSciences ICP monitoring (separate product, external)
buyer_2_integra_lifesciences.why_p_01_matters: Integra has BOTH a shunt product AND an ICP monitoring product, but they are NOT integrated. P-01 V2 could integrate sensing + control INTO the shunt itself — a product Integra doesn't have but their portfolio suggests they should.
buyer_2_integra_lifesciences.what_experiment_they_run: Run the V2 simulator to see if continuous control is feasible with their existing ICP sensor (Codman MicroSensor) integrated into a multi-segment catheter. The experiment tests whether their existing sensor + our control law = a viable next-gen product.
buyer_2_integra_lifesciences.what_data_they_provide: (1) Codman MicroSensor specifications (accuracy, drift, chronic implantation data). (2) Codman Hakim valve flow-pressure curves. (3) Their view on multi-segment catheter feasibility (manufacturing, regulatory).
buyer_2_integra_lifesciences.what_decision_they_make: 'Should we integrate our ICP sensor + a multi-segment catheter + P-01 V2 control law into a single next-gen product?' If the simulator shows V2 works with their sensor specs → internal product roadmap discussion.
buyer_2_integra_lifesciences.contact_strategy: LinkedIn to Head of R&D, CSF Management. Reference their dual portfolio (shunt + ICP monitor) and the integration opportunity. Offer simulator + their sensor specs as the first experiment.
buyer_2_integra_lifesciences.probability_of_engagement: 20-30% (Integra has the sensor + shunt combo, so the integration thesis is natural)

buyer_3_sophysa.existing_product: Sophysa Polaris (programmable valve, MRI-safe, adjustable) + Sophysa Shunt Assistant (gravity-assisted valve for over-drainage prevention)
buyer_3_sophysa.why_p_01_matters: Sophysa is a smaller, more agile European company. They have the engineering culture to evaluate a novel control law quickly. They also have a gravity-assisted valve (Shunt Assistant) which shows they think about dynamic drainage control. P-01 V2 is the next step: ACTIVE dynamic control instead of PASSIVE gravity-assisted.
buyer_3_sophysa.what_experiment_they_run: Run the V2 simulator to compare: (a) their Polaris fixed-setting, (b) their Shunt Assistant passive gravity control, (c) P-01 V2 active continuous control. The experiment shows whether active control adds value beyond their passive approach.
buyer_3_sophysa.what_data_they_provide: (1) Polaris valve specifications. (2) Shunt Assistant flow-pressure-gravity curves. (3) Their European market data on shunt obstruction rates (may differ from US data).
buyer_3_sophysa.what_decision_they_make: 'Should we develop an active control shunt (Polaris + sensors + P-01 V2) as our next-generation product?' If V2 outperforms their passive Shunt Assistant → product development conversation.
buyer_3_sophysa.contact_strategy: Direct email to CTO or Head of R&D. Sophysa is small enough that a direct technical email is appropriate. Reference their Shunt Assistant as evidence they understand dynamic drainage.
buyer_3_sophysa.probability_of_engagement: 25-35% (smaller company, faster decision-making, European engineering culture values rigorous technical evaluation)

buyer_4_christoph_miethke.division: R&D / proSA and proGAV valve product line
buyer_4_christoph_miethke.existing_product: proSA (adjustable differential pressure valve with gravitational unit) + proGAV (adjustable differential pressure valve) + Miethke SENSOR RESERVOIR (ICP sensor integrated into shunt reservoir — closest to P-01's hardware concept on the market)
buyer_4_christoph_miethke.why_p_01_matters: Miethke ALREADY has an ICP sensor integrated into a shunt reservoir (SENSOR RESERVOIR). This is the closest existing product to P-01's hardware concept. The missing piece is the CONTROL LAW — Miethke's sensor is for MONITORING, not for CLOSED-LOOP CONTROL. P-01 V2 provides the control law that turns their sensor into a closed-loop system.
buyer_4_christoph_miethke.what_experiment_they_run: Run the V2 simulator with their SENSOR RESERVOIR specs. Test whether V2's continuous control, using their existing sensor, outperforms their current 'monitor-only' approach. This is the highest-fit experiment because their hardware is closest to what P-01 needs.
buyer_4_christoph_miethke.what_data_they_provide: (1) SENSOR RESERVOIR specifications (accuracy, sampling rate, chronic implantation data). (2) proSA/proGAV valve specifications. (3) Their clinical data on sensor-based monitoring outcomes. (4) Their view on regulatory pathway for closed-loop control (they have the most experience with sensor-in-shunt products).
buyer_4_christoph_miethke.what_decision_they_make: 'Should we upgrade SENSOR RESERVOIR from monitoring-only to closed-loop control using P-01 V2?' This is the highest-probability path to a real product because the hardware already exists.
buyer_4_christoph_miethke.contact_strategy: Direct email to Head of R&D. Reference their SENSOR RESERVOIR specifically. The thesis is: 'You have the sensor. We have the control law. Together = closed-loop shunt.' This is the most compelling integration story in the portfolio.
buyer_4_christoph_miethke.probability_of_engagement: 30-40% (HIGHEST — they have the hardware, they have the engineering culture, they have the regulatory experience with sensor-in-shunt products)

buyer_5_academic_lab_stanford.division: Department of Neurosurgery / Pediatric Neurosurgery (Dr. Michael Edwards or equivalent PI)
buyer_5_academic_lab_stanford.existing_product: N/A (academic lab, but they have animal models, bench hydraulic simulators, and clinical data access)
buyer_5_academic_lab_stanford.why_p_01_matters: Academic labs provide INDEPENDENT VALIDATION — the constitutional requirement (Article XXVI) for moving from BUYER_READY_FOR_TECHNICAL_EVALUATION to INDEPENDENTLY_VALIDATED. Stanford Neurosurgery has the animal model capability and the clinical data to validate P-01 V2 beyond simulation.
buyer_5_academic_lab_stanford.what_experiment_they_run: (1) Run the V2 simulator independently — verify our findings. (2) Build the V0 bench prototype per our frozen protocol. (3) If bench validates: propose an animal model study (chronic hydrocephalus pig model) to test V2 in vivo.
buyer_5_academic_lab_stanford.what_data_they_provide: (1) Independent simulation results (confirm or refute our V2 vs B finding). (2) Bench prototype test results (30 runs, 720 bench-hours). (3) If they choose to proceed: animal model ICP and drainage data. (4) Their clinical shunt failure data (for the buyer economic questionnaire).
buyer_5_academic_lab_stanford.what_decision_they_make: 'Does P-01 V2 survive independent validation?' If YES → co-author a paper, which becomes the first EXTERNAL evidence in the package. If NO → the package is falsified by an independent party (the strongest possible negative result).
buyer_5_academic_lab_stanford.contact_strategy: Email to PI directly. Reference the external validation handoff folder (frozen design, frozen protocol, pre-registered acceptance criteria). Offer to ship the bench prototype spec. No cost to the lab beyond their time.
buyer_5_academic_lab_stanford.probability_of_engagement: 15-25% (academic labs are busy, but the offer of a well-specified validation package with pre-registered criteria is attractive to PIs who want publishable negative or positive results)

engagement_sequence.step_1: Send tailored outreach to Buyer 4 (Miethke) FIRST — highest probability, best hardware fit. If they engage, the SENSOR RESERVOIR integration story becomes the lead commercial thesis.
engagement_sequence.step_2: Send to Buyer 3 (Sophysa) — second highest probability, agile company, European engineering culture.
engagement_sequence.step_3: Send to Buyer 2 (Integra) — they have both sensor and shunt, integration thesis is natural.
engagement_sequence.step_4: Send to Buyer 5 (Stanford) — academic validation path, slower but provides INDEPENDENTLY_VALIDATED state.
engagement_sequence.step_5: Send to Buyer 1 (Medtronic) LAST — largest company, slowest decision, but biggest commercial impact if they engage.
engagement_sequence.timeline: Send all 5 within 2 weeks. First responses expected within 1-4 weeks. First technical evaluation conversation within 4-8 weeks.
engagement_sequence.success_criterion: At least 1 of 5 buyers responds with 'Send me the package; we'll run it.' That is the first commercial evidence event.
